purpose: Each entry names one load-bearing behaviour, the exact source edit that removes it, and the witness that must turn red once it is gone. A witness that stays green under its own mutation attributes nothing.
isolation: Every mutation is applied inside its own disposable git worktree checked out at the exact candidate commit. No mutant is ever written into the calling worktree, so a restore step cannot silently leave a stale build behind.

tombstones.law: The fetch path re-verified that the record reproduces the reference identity
tombstones.reason: UNREACHABLE, not descoped. L3 moved identity reproduction into stat, and stat looks the record up BY the reference id and refuses unless the record id equals both that key and the identity recomputed from (kind, disposition, length, digest). By the time fetch runs, reference.id == meta.id == expected holds unconditionally, so the fetch-side copy could never fire. It went GREEN under its own mutation, which is how it was found; the branch was deleted rather than left as unwitnessed code. See crates/grapt-artifact/src/fs.rs where the branch used to be.

note_on_the_comment_route: Review asked for the trailing-comment bypass to be self-witnessed with a right-reason mutation. It IS a self-witnessed route in the_gate_catches_every_bypass_form, but there is deliberately NO mutation descriptor for it, and faking one would misrepresent why it is closed. The hand-rolled scanner failed that route because it reasoned about LINES; structural TOML parsing removes the line-shaped code entirely, so there is no line-recognition step left to delete. The class is unrepresentable rather than policed, which is stronger than a witness. A22 and A23 instead mutate the two decisions the parser really does make — which tables it reads, and whether it resolves a package alias.
